iciness_notes: Noticeably icy after 24h. Ice crystals visible on the palate. PAC likely too low for the water content.
body_notes: Good body and overrun. Melts evenly.
overall_notes: Promising base flavour but texture lets it down after storage. Try shifting some sucrose to dextrose and adding trehalose to depress freezing point without over-sweetening.

iciness_notes: No detectable iciness even after 48h. Trehalose made a clear difference.
body_notes: Slightly creamier than v1. Scoops cleanly at -14°C.
overall_notes: Big improvement. The trehalose slows recrystallisation without adding excessive sweetness — its low POD (45) keeps the flavour balanced. This base will carry other flavours well.

iciness_notes: Good texture fresh from the machine. Harder than ideal after overnight freeze — sorbet loses flexibility faster than cream-based mixes.
body_notes: Light, clean mouthfeel appropriate for sorbet. Good meltdown.
overall_notes: Best flavour of any batch so far — the strawberry is vivid and fresh. The glucose syrup adds elasticity which helps. Next iteration: increase PAC by ~2% and serve slightly warmer (-10°C).

iciness_notes: Zero iciness. Velvety throughout. The invert sugar contributes noticeably to smoothness.
body_notes: Rich, dense body. Melts slowly and evenly. Best mouthfeel to date.
overall_notes: Best batch overall. The invert sugar adds a silkiness that's hard to describe — likely due to its hygroscopic properties slowing ice crystal growth. Flavour is deep and complex. Appearance could be more glossy; may try adding cocoa butter next time.

iciness_notes: Slight iciness after 72h but nothing distracting. Caramelised sugars may behave differently to raw sucrose.
body_notes: Excellent body. The caramel gives a slightly denser texture than vanilla base.
overall_notes: Added fleur de sel after churning rather than in the mix — creates bursts of salt in eating rather than uniform background saltiness. Beautiful amber colour. Strong result for a first attempt at this flavour.
